summary: Retest of the iteration_28 fixes, run at 390x844 as user_avatar_test with /app/tests/cam_mock_avatar.js and cam_mock_lens.js. (1) LEG_FRAC [0.47,0.60]: PASS. The good upper+lower pair is no longer clamped: inseam_r 0.4954, leg_frac 0.576. POST /api/profile/avatar is sent with features and returns 76/66/90/33/83, exactly the iteration_27 result. Stitched image is 960x1496 and looks natural. Against single-shot (79/67/91/35/80): chest -3.8%, waist -1.5%, hips -1.1%, inseam +3.75%, all within 5%. Shoulder is the exception: 33 vs 35 = -5.7%, the same as in iteration_27. (2) No-anchor fallback: PARTIAL PASS. With lower photo x1.3 and x1.6 the result is 960x1363, down from 960x2000. Legs are no longer very long and no longer extend down the page. Visual problems remain (see ui_bugs): the whole lower frame is uniformly shrunk to fit a 0.53 leg length, so the lower body is about 55-60% of the torso's width. The waist-to-hip band of photo 2, including the hand on the hip, is drawn a second time just below the seam. Photo 2's white rectangle is narrower than the upper frame, which leaves a visible box edge. (3) Italian iOS labels: PASS. The default stream is 'Fotocamera tripla posteriore'; a second getUserMedia call uses deviceId exact back-id and opens 'Fotocamera posteriore'. Zoom 1 is applied, and the live video track label is 'Fotocamera posteriore'. Front 'Fotocamera anteriore' uses a single getUserMedia call (no switch). Flipping back in double mode switches to back-id again. 'doppia grandangolare', 'ultra grandangolare' and 'teleobiettivo' are never selected. (4) no_measure with height saved: the code fix is PASS, the outcome is FAIL. Confirm now sends POST /api/profile/quick-estimate {height_cm:168, weight_kg:60, gender:'female'} (200) before POST /api/profile/avatar, and the toast 'Avatar salvato: misure stimate da altezza e peso' appears. However, the backend returns kept_precise=true because height, weight and gender are unchanged and the method is auto_photo. Measurements therefore stay at the old photo values (method auto_photo, precision 98), and the toast is still untruthful. The required 'method becomes quick estimate' does NOT happen. No avatar-photo-issue appeared in any 2-shot run, no page errors occurred, and every save succeeded.

ui_bugs.issue: s = (0.53*upperH/0.47)/l.H scales the WHOLE lower frame, including the top margin and the waist-to-hip band, to the leg length. Results: (a) the lower body is about 0.55-0.6x narrower than the torso, giving a 'small legs' look; (b) the dress band and the hand on the hip from photo 2 are repeated below the seam; (c) the lower frame (l.W*s, about 530px) is narrower than W=960, so a visible rectangular edge appears on the backdrop. Not stretched any more, but the proportions are still wrong. Compare /tmp/it29_cmp.jpg (good | x1.3 | x1.6).

integration_issues.issue: The frontend now calls /profile/quick-estimate, but backend quick_estimate keeps auto_photo/tape measurements when height, weight and gender are unchanged (kept_precise=true). The method stays auto_photo with precision 98, while the toast says 'misure stimate da altezza e peso'. Also, the new avatar photo (unmeasurable) now sits next to precision-98 measurements taken from an older photo.

action_items: AvatarBox.upload or backend: make no_measure truthful. Either (a) add a force flag to /profile/quick-estimate, e.g. {force:true} that skips the 'keep' branch when called from the no_measure path; or (b) read resp.data.kept_precise and show a toast such as 'Avatar salvato: misure precedenti mantenute' when it is true. Pick one approach and make the toast match what actually happened.

pose.js no-anchor fallback: do not shrink the whole lower frame to the leg length. Use the horizontal scale of the upper frame (s = u.W/l.W, or a width estimated from u's hip span) and crop or cover the top part of photo 2 (about l.H*0.15-0.25, the waist band) so it is not drawn again. Alternatively, if l.p exists with partial landmarks, use l.bottom/l.top. Fill the area outside the lower frame with the sampled backdrop color, or use dx = 0 with full width, so no box edge shows.
Optional: the shoulder in 2-shot is about 5.7% under single-shot (33 vs 35), unchanged since iteration_27.
critical_code_review_comments: pose.js line 233 still has the old comment 'simply stack photo 2 under photo 1' directly above the new comment. Remove the stale line.

openNormalLens still forces zoom:1 even when no physical normal lens is found. On iOS virtual multi-camera devices this may lock the 0.5x lens (risk raised in iteration_28; still not verified on a device).
The no-anchor fallback uses the constant 0.53/0.47, while keepRealProportions uses LEG_FRAC [0.47,0.6]. Consider a single shared constant.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The browser_automation script is in /app/tests/it29_stitch.py (inline it). It reads /tmp images, injects the mocks and wraps URL.createObjectURL to capture the stitched blob (skip the non-image blob with try/catch on createImageBitmap). For Italian labels, set window.__devs and __defaultLabel before the mocks. The stitched outputs are saved to /tmp/it29_{good,s13,str}.jpg, and /tmp/it29_cmp.jpg is a side-by-side comparison. leg_frac = inseam_r/0.86.
rca of the issue: no_measure untruthful: server.py quick_estimate sets keep=True when the method is auto_photo/tape and height (within 1 cm), weight (within 5 kg) and gender are unchanged. The frontend sends exactly the saved values, so keep is always true in this path and nothing is re-estimated. Fallback proportions: with no anchor, the scale is derived from the full lower frame height (l.H) rather than the legs' pixel extent, and the frame top (waist and hips) is placed at u.hipY.
